calls.reason: Bain estimates $2 trillion under continued scaling and projected demand. That conditional industry scenario does not establish what hyperscalers necessarily need for their spending to make financial sense.
Anthropic's filing reports losses and positive adjusted operating income, but neither establishes sustainable prices. The packet shows no customer response to verified cost-covering pricing.

Menlo estimates $37 billion in enterprise spending, covering only part of the claimed market. It supplies no cost evidence showing whether demand depends on subsidies or would disappear at sustainable prices.

Anthropic and GIC corroborate the $30 billion round and date. GIC cites technical capabilities and enterprise adoption, but the packet does not establish whether the publicity campaign helped secure funding.

Bloomberg documents credit concerns, but the memorandum distinguishes a $40 billion facility from actual borrowing, and the LTV breach was projected. The evidence does not settle the judgment that SoftBank was very precariously positioned.

Cursor links pricing changes to token costs but reports no resulting departures. Lindy reports cheaper inference with retention holding, leaving the claimed general chain from rising costs to churn unclear.
